chapters.title: Every Spiritual Blessing
chapters.html:
Ephesians 1

Greeting

1Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, to the saints who are in Ephesus, the faithful in Christ Jesus:

2Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

Every Spiritual Blessing in Christ

3Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places,

4even as He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, to be holy and without defect before Him in love.

5He appointed us beforehand for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ, to be His own, according to the good pleasure of His will,

6to the praise of the glory of His grace, with which He has graced us in the Beloved.

7In Him we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of His grace,

8which He lavished on us in all wisdom and understanding,

9making known to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure, which He purposed in Him

10as a plan for the fullness of the times: to sum up all things in Christ, the things in the heavens and the things on the earth. In Him

11we too were made His portion, having been appointed beforehand according to the purpose of Him who works all things according to the counsel of His will,

12so that we who were the first to hope in Christ might be to the praise of His glory.

13In Him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in Him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit,

14who is the pledge of our inheritance, until the redemption of God's own possession, to the praise of His glory.

Paul's Prayer

15For this reason I too, having heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,

16do not stop giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers,

17that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the Spirit of wisdom and revelation in the knowledge of Him,

18having the eyes of your heart enlightened, so that you may know what is the hope of His calling, what are the riches of the glory of His inheritance in the saints,

19and what is the surpassing greatness of His power toward us who believe, according to the working of His mighty strength,

20which He worked in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,

21far above every ruler and authority and power and dominion, and above every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come.

22He put all things under His feet and gave Him as head over all things to the church,

23which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all in all.

Notes

  • v1 "who are in Ephesus" — the edition prints en Ephesō in square brackets, its mark for words it is not sure belong to the text. The letter itself names no one in the city and sends no greetings.

  • v4 "holy and without defect before Him" — amōmos, the word the Greek Bible uses for an offering: it must be without defect to be accepted (Leviticus 22:21), amōmon in the Greek. Paul uses it again of the church, presented holy and without defect (5:27), and it is the word for Christ, who offered Himself without defect to God (Hebrews 9:14).

  • vv4, 6 "He chose us in Him… with which He has graced us in the Beloved" — ho ēgapēmenos, the Beloved, is Israel's name in the Greek Bible, where the Hebrew has Jeshurun: Do not fear, Jacob My servant, and the beloved Israel whom I have chosen (Isaiah 44:2; also Deuteronomy 32:15; 33:5, 26). Here the Beloved is Christ, and the ones chosen are chosen in Him. Echaritōsen, graced, is used once more in the New Testament: Gabriel's Greetings, favored one! to Mary (Luke 1:28).

  • v10 "to sum up all things in Christ" — anakephalaiōsasthai, from kephalaion, the sum or main point, the word of Romans 13:9, where every commandment is summed up in love your neighbor. Kephalaion itself comes from kephalē, head, and twelve verses on God gives Christ as head over all things (v22): all things summed up in Him, or brought together under Him as head.

  • vv11, 14, 18 "we too were made His portion… God's own possession… His inheritance in the saints" — eklērōthēmen, from klēros, a lot or allotted share, is passive: the believers are made God's share, or are given a share of their own (our inheritance, v14). The thought is Moses' song, the LORD's portion is His people, Jacob the measured lot of His inheritance (Deuteronomy 32:9), and peripoiēsis, possession, is Malachi's They will be Mine… My own treasure (Malachi 3:17), eis peripoiēsin in the Greek. So in v18 the inheritance is God's own, in the saints.

  • vv20–22 "seated Him at His right hand… He put all things under His feet" — two psalms, as in 1 Corinthians 15:25–27: Sit at My right hand (Psalm 110:1) and You have put all things under his feet (Psalm 8:6), the psalm of what God made a human being to be.

chapters.title: One New Man
chapters.html:
Ephesians 2

Alive with Christ

1As for you, you were dead in your trespasses and sins,

2in which you once walked, following the course of this world, following the ruler of the authority of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience.

3Among them we too all once lived in the desires of our flesh, carrying out the wishes of the flesh and of the mind, and we were by nature children of wrath, like the rest.

4But God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which He loved us,

5even when we were dead in our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ — by grace you have been saved —

6and raised us up with Him and seated us with Him in the heavenly places in Christ Jesus,

7so that in the ages to come He might show the surpassing riches of His grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.

8For by grace you have been saved through faith; and this is not from yourselves; it is the gift of God,

9not from works, so that no one may boast.

10For we are what He has made, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them.

One New Man

11So remember that at one time you, the Gentiles in the flesh, called "the uncircumcision" by those called "the circumcision," which is made in the flesh by hands —

12remember that you were at that time without Christ, shut out from the citizenship of Israel and strangers to the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world.

13But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ.

14For He Himself is our peace, who has made the two one and has broken down the dividing wall, the hostility, in His flesh,

15by abolishing the law of commandments expressed in decrees, so that He might create in Himself one new man out of the two, so making peace,

16and might reconcile both to God in one body through the cross, having put the hostility to death by it.

17He came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near,

18for through Him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father.

19So then you are no longer strangers and guests, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God,

20built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus Himself being the cornerstone,

21in whom the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord,

22in whom you also are being built together into a dwelling place of God in the Spirit.

Notes

  • vv13, 17 "you who once were far off have been brought near… He came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near" — Isaiah's word, Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says the LORD, and I will heal him (Isaiah 57:19). In Isaiah the promise is to the LORD's own people, the one who is crushed and lowly in spirit (57:15); Paul makes the far the Gentiles, brought near by the blood of Christ.

  • v20 "Christ Jesus Himself being the cornerstone" — akrogōniaios, the word of the Greek of Isaiah 28:16, I am laying in Zion a stone… a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. The stone Isaiah lays in Zion's foundation is the stone the whole building is joined to, Gentiles and Jews together.
